subject: System Design
title: Rebalancing Partitions
description: A fast breakdown of Rebalancing Partitions for builders.

hook.text: Your cluster grows from 5 to 10 nodes. How do you redistribute data without taking the system down?

buildup.text: Rebalancing moves partitions between nodes to distribute load evenly after cluster changes.

discovery.text: Fixed partition count is simplest: create more partitions than nodes. New nodes take over whole partitions.

twist.text: Moving data between nodes uses network bandwidth. If done too aggressively, it saturates the network.

climax.text: Good rebalancing is invisible to users. Bad rebalancing causes outages during the migration.

punchline.text: Rebalance gradually — or crash under the load.

quiz.question: Why should rebalancing be done gradually?
options: Aggressive data movement saturates the network
